Definition: from (the reduplicated form of) G4863; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church:--assembly, congregation, synagogue.
KeyPassages: Luke 4:16; Mark 1:21; Matthew 4:23; John 18:20; Acts 17:1; Revelation 2:9
BiblicalUsage: Jesus goes into the synagogue on the sabbath, as His custom was, and stands up to read, and He teaches in their synagogues all through Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom. He tells the high priest He always taught in the synagogue and the temple, openly, and said nothing in secret, and Paul's custom is the same: wherever he comes, he goes first to the synagogue of the Jews. Yet John also writes of those who say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, so the same building can hold true worship or its counterfeit.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the synagogue was where Jesus was at home, teaching openly on the sabbath, and I believe the place matters less than the truth taught in it. I take the warning seriously too: a gathering can wear God's name and serve Satan, so I must test what is taught, not only where it is taught.
RelatedBooks: Luke; Mark; Matthew; John; Acts; Revelation
